# Derivation 3.6A — Stationary correspondence calibration {#sec-derivation-03-06A-stationary-correspondence .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix calibrates the native stationary source and scalar field against
ordinary weak-field variables, then separates achieved correspondence from
unclosed light and directional targets.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** downstream calibration and regression ledger.
- **Regime:** weak, stationary, asymptotically flat overlap.
- **Status:** density dimensions, Newtonian normalization, and scalar clock
  redshift are established within the adopted stationary map. PPN
  $\gamma=1$ and the physical directional sector remain targets.
- **Non-claim:** agreement with the Newtonian limit is not a derivation of the
  full GR metric or its field equations.

## Source dimensions

The native even source is a momentum-content density,

$$
[\mathcal M]=\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}m^{-2}},
$$

whereas ordinary mass density has units $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Cold static
matter therefore calibrates as

$$
\boxed{\mathcal M=c\rho}.
\tag{3.6A.1}
$$

For later time-dependent notation it is convenient to define, before use,

$$
\rho_M:=\frac{\mathcal M}{c}.
\tag{3.6A.2}
$$

$t_*$ denotes the action evolution time normalized to the asymptotic clock.

The first and second carrier moments face the classical momentum-form ledger
as

$$
P^{\mu\nu}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathcal M & \mathcal P_j\\
\mathcal P_i & \mathcal C_{ij}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
T^{\mu\nu}=cP^{\mu\nu}
\tag{3.6A.3}
$$

in the local flat comparison convention. Equation (3.6A.3) is a dictionary,
not the primitive M1 source law.

## Newtonian recovery

The stationary scalar equation is

$$
\Delta\theta_0=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}\mathcal M.
$$

With Equation (3.6A.1),

$$
\Delta\theta_0=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^2}\rho.
$$

The dimensionally correct potential dictionary is

$$
\boxed{\theta_0\longleftrightarrow-\frac U{c^2}},
\qquad
U:=-c^2\theta_0,
\tag{3.6A.4}
$$

so

$$
\Delta U=4\pi G_N\rho.
$$

For a spherical source of mass $M$,

$$
U(r)=-\frac{G_NM}{r},
\qquad
\theta_0(r)=\frac{G_NM}{c^2r}.
$$

The selected scalar clock factor

$$
G=\sqrt{1-2\theta_0}
=1+\frac U{c^2}+O(U^2/c^4)
$$

therefore has the standard leading clock-redshift slope. The exact square root
is a resummation of this selected clock package, not a nonlinear spatial
closure.

## Spatial and light correspondence target

Write the weak isotropic ruler as

$$
d\ell^2=
\left(1-2\gamma\frac U{c^2}\right)
\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j.
\tag{3.6A.5}
$$

Then the leading light coefficients are

$$
\delta\phi
=2(1+\gamma)\frac{G_NM}{bc^2},
$$

$$
\Delta t_{\mathrm{Shapiro}}
=\frac{(1+\gamma)G_NM}{c^3}
\ln(\text{endpoint geometry}).
\tag{3.6A.6}
$$

Observations require the standard $\gamma=1$ values
[@will2014confrontation]. Derivations 3.4B and
3.4C show that the current content-only source and a reciprocal
$\gamma=1$ ruler are not jointly action-closed in the reviewed carrier and
regular self-adjoint response class. Equations (3.6A.5)--(3.6A.6) are
therefore correspondence requirements, not predictions of a closed M1
spatial action.

## Directional target

Given $\mathcal P_i=j_i$, the inherited transverse field-side equation is

$$
\Delta\theta_i^\perp
=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}j_i^\perp.
$$

Weak Kerr/Lense--Thirring comparison requires a metric- or
observer-facing response of magnitude four relative to $\theta_i^\perp$ in
the conventions of Derivation 3.6B. The sign-bearing action-to-observer map is
not closed, so no physical equality between a particular action coordinate
and the metric shift is asserted here.

## Result

Chapter 3 has an achieved weak stationary scalar calibration:

$$
\mathcal M=c\rho,
\qquad
\theta_0=-U/c^2,
\qquad
\Delta U=4\pi G_N\rho.
$$

Standard weak spatial light response and the rotating-source shift remain
explicit regression targets with unresolved action/readout premises.
